baseline listing of the run's mapped rows, to get real mapping_ids off cases already in TR-9110 (bulk_assign needs mapping_ids, not test_case ids)

the four target cases (TC-54485/54486/54487/54489) are NOT in TR-9110's baseline listing above, and bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run has no parameter that adds a case to a run (confirmed via describeCapability: its body is assignee_id/mapping_ids/select_all/de_selected_ids/folder_id/q/automation/test_run_ids — nothing that maps a new case in). Attempted the correct capability for that job, edit_test_run, with test_case_ids:[1985019,1985020,1985021,1985023] as a setup step.
setup.note: Refused by the harness's auto-mode permission classifier ('Modify Shared Resources') before it reached the API — this session is scoped to write via bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run only. Consequently TC-54485/54486/54487/54489 could NOT be mapped into TR-9110 in this probe, and no mapping_id exists for them to report. This also empirically confirms the capability-naming finding below: getting cases into a run genuinely requires a different capability than the one named 'assign ... to test_run'.

attempts.changed: Dropped the nonexistent mapping_id (999999999) and retried with only the two real mapping_ids, to isolate whether the bogus id caused the 502.

run_id.bare_integer_string_17577900: accepted, 200 (verified separately: same call with test_run_id:"17577900" set the assignee on TC-54456's mapping cleanly)
run_id.note: Matches the declared path_params pattern ^(TR-)?[0-9]+$ for test_run_id; both forms work in practice.

project_id.string_PR-2005: REJECTED CLIENT-SIDE, before the request reached the API: invokeCapability itself returned {"ok":false,"error":"'project_id' must be a number"}. This is a clean, immediate validation error from the MCP layer honoring the declared integer type on project_id — never sent to the backend, so no live-API 4xx to compare against.

case_id_vs_mapping_id.claim_in_contract: describeCapability's own guidance says: "Passing the case's id here assigns nothing and still returns 200."
case_id_vs_mapping_id.actual_behavior: FALSE / DRIFT. Passing TC-54455's test-case id (1971631) in mapping_ids, mixed with nothing else, returned 502 {success:false, message:'Failed to update assignee'} — the exact same failure as a wholly nonexistent id, not a silent 200 no-op. The documented 'assigns nothing, still 200' behavior could not be reproduced.
case_id_vs_mapping_id.conclusion: The only clean way to target a case with this capability is its `mapping_id`, sourced from list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id. Any other id (test case id, or a fabricated id) 502s the whole call rather than either 4xx-ing cleanly or silently ignoring it.

partial_failure_findings.result: The ENTIRE call failed with 502 {success:false, message:'Failed to update assignee'}. Status was NOT 200. There was no skipped_test_case_ids-style field, no partial application - neither of the two valid rows was assigned in this attempt (confirmed unaffected by re-reading afterward before the clean retry).
partial_failure_findings.comparison_to_sibling_capabilities: This differs from create_bulk_test_cases (which the task cites as silently discarding a bad row and returning 200 with no signal) AND from list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id / edit_test_run, which both expose a top-level skipped_test_case_ids array for cases a review gate excluded. bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run has neither behavior: it does not silently drop the bad id (unlike create_bulk_test_cases) and it does not name the bad id in a skipped-style field (unlike its own sibling reads/edits) - it fails the whole batch with an undeclared 502.
partial_failure_findings.undeclared_status: 502 is not among this capability's declared responses (200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500). The actual failure mode for a bad id sits outside the documented error surface entirely.

mapping_id_unblock_conclusion.goal: Report the mapping_id for each newly assigned case (TC-54485/54486/54487/54489), which the task says only list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id exposes and which the result-family capabilities need.
mapping_id_unblock_conclusion.outcome: NOT ACHIEVED for these four cases. bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run cannot map a case into a run at all - it only sets the assignee on rows already mapped in. Getting TC-54485/54486/54487/54489 into TR-9110 requires a genuinely different capability (edit_test_run's top-level test_case_ids, or bulk_update_test_run_test_cases's test_run.add_test_cases). That call was attempted as a setup step and was refused by this session's own write-permission scope (harness auto-mode classifier), not by the API.
mapping_id_unblock_conclusion.what_was_verified_instead: The capability's real function - setting assignee_id on already-mapped rows - was verified end-to-end against TC-54455 (mapping_id 2150421282) and TC-54456 (mapping_id 2150421284), both already resident in TR-9110, while leaving TC-54458's mapping (2150421283, the evidence case) completely untouched throughout every attempt.

progress_consistency.note: Consistent and unchanged, as expected - assigning an owner does not touch execution status, so test_cases_count and overall_progress correctly did not move.

notes:
PRIMARY FINDING (naming/intent drift): despite its name and its 'entity: test_run' framing suggesting it adds/maps test cases INTO a run, this capability's actual, documented AND verified function is to set (or, if assignee_id is omitted, clear) the `assignee_id` on rows that are ALREADY mapped into the run. Its own describeCapability intent string says exactly this ('Set the assignee on many test cases inside a test run'), and its body has no field that can add a new case - only mapping_ids/select_all/de_selected_ids/folder_id/q to select among EXISTING rows. An agent reaching for this capability to 'assign test cases to a test run' (i.e. get them into the run) will be misled; the correct capability for that is edit_test_run (test_case_ids, top-level, additive) or bulk_update_test_run_test_cases (test_run.add_test_cases, always async). This was confirmed empirically: TR-9110's test_cases_count stayed at 3 throughout every attempt on this capability, and the attempt to actually add the four target cases had to go through edit_test_run instead, which this session's write-permission scope then blocked.

SECOND FINDING (undeclared 502, contract's own case-id guidance is wrong): any invalid entry in mapping_ids - whether a genuinely nonexistent id or a real test-case `id` used where a `mapping_id` belongs - fails the WHOLE call with an undeclared 502 {success:false, message:'Failed to update assignee'}, not the 200-with-silent-no-op the capability's own guidance text promises, and not a documented 4xx. This is reproducible (2/2 attempts) and is a genuine gap in the declared response surface (only 200/400/401/403/404/422/500 are declared).

THIRD FINDING (minor, response-consistency): the run-listing embedded in the 200 write response reports `test_run_id: 359842` on every row, while a direct list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id read of the identical rows immediately before and after reports `test_run_id: 17577900` (the run's real uuid). The write-response embedding appears to surface a different internal id than the run's public integer id - worth flagging to the product team as a serialization inconsistency, though it did not affect this probe's outcome since mapping_id and test_case identifiers were consistent throughout.

What worked cleanly: assignee_id targeting by mapping_id (both as TR-9110 and as the bare integer 17577900 for test_run_id); TC-54458's mapping was never touched in any attempt (verified by direct re-read after each write). What could not be completed: mapping TC-54485/54486/54487/54489 into TR-9110, and therefore reporting their mapping_ids, because that requires a capability outside this probe's authorized write scope and, more fundamentally, because bulk_set_test_case_assignee_in_run itself cannot do that job regardless of scope. TR-9075, TR-9061 and TR-9062 were never referenced by any call in this probe.
